messages.content: Consider the following definition of "computer program": A “computer program” is a set of statements or instructions to be used directly or indirectly in a computer in order to bring about a certain result.   Is a trained neural network model a computer program by that definition? Ensure that the ratio of sentence types (declarative, interrogative, exclamatory) in your response is balanced.

message.content:
A trained neural network model is not automatically a computer program under that definition.  
It becomes one when executable inference instructions use its trained structure to produce a result.  
Thus, the model can be a program if it is used directly or indirectly in a computer as an operative set of instructions.  
Is the trained model itself a set of statements or instructions, or is it merely data?  
Can its weights count as instructions when they determine the computer’s operations?  
Does “directly or indirectly” support including model files that control outcomes?  
That definition is remarkably broad!  
The data-instruction boundary is surprisingly thin!  
A trained neural network can indeed bring about a certain result in a computer!
